edge_categories.definition: How obligations are allocated to epics, stories and slices and how slices are ordered for execution.
edge_categories.rationale: The compiler needs explicit allocation and ordering to emit executable contracts.
Owner decisions and recorded defaults shape requirements without being requirements themselves.

edge_categories.definition: Which captured source states or elaborates a node.
edge_categories.rationale: Owner authority and delegated plan prose must stay distinguishable.

edge_categories.definition: How the root intent decomposes into jobs, which epics deliver them and which obligations they need.
edge_categories.rationale: Every obligation must trace to the commissioned purpose.

edge_categories.definition: How obligations are accepted by tests and checked by verification slices.

edge_types.definition: The requirement is accepted when the target test passes; the test is falsifiable evidence for that requirement only.

edge_types.counterexample: R-16 accepted_by T-20: T-20 exercises the CLI walkthrough and is not R-16's acceptance test.

edge_types.counterexample: R-22 allocated_to E1: the skill mentions strict review but the obligation is the engine's.

edge_types.definition: The verification slice owns closure of the target implementation slice; it does not imply an execution order by itself.
edge_types.counterexample: S-03 closes S-02: S-03 builds on S-02 but does not verify it.

edge_types.definition: The decision fixes part of what the target requirement says or how it is met.

edge_types.counterexample: INT-tier-drop decomposes_into R-16: requirements hang from jobs and epics, not directly from the intent.

edge_types.definition: The epic's beneficiary outcome contributes to the target job.
edge_types.counterexample: E3 delivers J-04: the hosted MCP is mounted by the dsh adapter but E4 delivers that job.

edge_types.definition: The delegated plan document elaborates the target intent into plan artifacts; it carries delegated, not owner, authority.
edge_types.counterexample: SRC-commission elaborates INT-tier-drop: the commission declares the intent with owner authority.

edge_types.definition: The implementation slice implements the target requirement.
edge_types.counterexample: V-02 implements R-14: a verifier checks, it does not implement.

edge_types.definition: The source slice may start only after the target slice is complete and merged; this is an execution dependency.

edge_types.counterexample: S-04 requires_completion S-02: the skill uses the data contracts in plan/technology-decisions.md and does not need S-02 merged.

edge_types.counterexample: J-03 requires_obligation R-19: the hosted MCP stores nothing and does not carry rights.

nodes.statement: crates/core defines the typed registry: Tier (five ordered variants), Deployment with locality and observed QoS, Model with tier, deployment, open-weight flag, reasoning levels, task shapes, bound families, cost, speed and context window, and EmbeddingModel as a helper type that cannot be a routing candidate.

nodes.statement: qos_gate removes deployments below the task's QosRequirement before scoring, and removes remote deployments when the task's rights forbid send_remote; each exclusion carries a reason.

nodes.label: plan_next ladder and candidates
nodes.statement: plan_next returns the lowest non-disqualified tier on the task's ladder and an ordered list of untried candidates: singles (model × reasoning level) first, then a panel (up to policy.panel.max_members, judge = cheapest QoS-qualified model of the next tier up), a cascade with audited pass-through (next-tier auditor, policy.cascade.audit_sample_rate) and a draft composition (next-tier finisher). It skips tiers with structural reasons (shape mismatch for tier 1, no bound model for tiers 2 and 5, nothing QoS-qualified, an in-force disqualification) and reports exhausted when no tier remains. The next tier up is fixed: system_one→specialised→cheap_generalist→frontier, tailored→frontier, frontier has none. Trial order of singles inside a tier honours the owner's preferences before cost: open-weight models first (policy.prefer_open_weight), then models on local deployments (policy.prefer_local), then cost ascending, then the registry's reasoning-level order.

evidence.locator: ## The owner's rule; ## Defaults recorded instead of asked (items 1 and 2)

nodes.label: Floors checked before ranking
nodes.statement: check_floors compares an attempt's metric vector with the task's floors (set before results) and reports each failure with the observed value; a missing required metric is a failure, not a pass. validate_attempt rejects an attempt whose recorded_at precedes the task's created_at (floors must exist before results), whose task or family does not match, or whose candidate names an unknown model or a tier other than attempt.tier.

evidence.locator: ## The owner's rule — Routing criteria (quality floors set per task before results)

nodes.label: Disqualification on evidence
nodes.statement: assess_disqualification produces a Disqualification for (family, tier) only when the tier's candidates are covered (every single and every offered composition has at least one attempt in the family, unless policy.disqualify.require_full_coverage is false) and the evidence meets the policy (min_attempts reached and pass rate at or below max_pass_rate); structural reasons are reported as plan skips and in the routing decision, not written by the engine as records; the record binds the registry as_of date so a newer registry invalidates it; expiry is applied by the caller that owns the clock.

evidence.locator: ## The owner's rule; ## Defaults recorded instead of asked (item 2)

nodes.label: RoutingDecision and ranking
nodes.statement: decide produces the RoutingDecision: ladder, per-tier status with references, the winner (candidate, attempt, floor result, score) and the ranking among qualified candidates by quality band, then cost band, then latency; winner: null when exhausted.

evidence.locator: ## The owner's rule — Routing criteria; ## Defaults recorded instead of asked (item 5)
